roadmaps.focus: weighted interpolation, factorization, ramification cleanup, and characteristic-safe propagation

messages.body_markdown: The round-3 relation branch now needs only total accepted mass. From `AE-12`, `AE-16` allocates lines to at most $K_\theta$ factors, `AE-17` pays the factorwise ramification budget, and `AE-18` obtains a simple high-direction seed by averaging point degrees. No inherited minimum degree or degree-$D$ peeling is required; please retain the mass-only certificate.
messages.subject: Mass-only handoff closes the factor branch

messages.body_markdown: `AE-19` gives the requested standalone simple-seed lift with $\Delta\le D<p$. Formal implicit uniqueness identifies the degree-$d$ truncation with every supplied line label; then $C(X,Y,Q)$ has degree at most $\Delta$ and more than $\Delta$ distinct line factors, so irreducibility gives $C\sim Z-Q$. The simple seed remains essential by `AE-11`.
messages.subject: Characteristic-safe simple-pencil lift

messages.body_markdown: The bounded-weight hypothesis performs two distinct jobs. It makes the uniform factorwise loss $$(D^2/d-D)/(p(p+1))+(D-d)/p$$ negligible relative to $\epsilon$, and it bounds the number of $Z$-dependent factors by $D/d\le K_\theta$. An inverse power of $\epsilon$ in $D/d$ breaks both `AE-17` and `AE-18`.
messages.subject: Both bounded-weight uses are indispensable

messages.body_markdown: New corpus evidence reinforces that `AE-12` must be label-aware. `AE-23` records a connected full-support carrier attaining all star-moment lower envelopes and requiring fractional reaching weight $\Theta(p/\epsilon)$ even though $Q=0$ decodes globally. `AE-24` supplies a stronger asymmetric decoder, but its interpolation scale still has the square-root gate and does not yield $D=O_\theta(d)$.
messages.subject: New corpus preserves the rank-or-decode obligation

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence instance
nodes.notes: This fixes the bivariate prime-field regime and excludes both dimension bootstrapping and $d\le100$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, and $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$. For every affine line $L$, fix a bijective affine parametrization $\ell_L:\mathbb F_p\to L$ and $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$. Put $$\mathcal I=\{(\ell_L(t),L):P_L(t)=f(\ell_L(t))\},\qquad \mu(E)=|E|/[p^2(p+1)],\qquad \epsilon=\mu(\mathcal I),$$ and let $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)$ be the maximum of $p^{-2}|\{x:Q(x)=f(x)\}|$ over $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$.

nodes.label: Weighted restriction map
nodes.notes: This is the Lean-level linear map measuring labeled graph constraints.
nodes.statement_markdown: Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $1,1,d$. For an integer $D\ge d$, put $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}A\le D\},\qquad \rho_L(A)(t)=A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t)).$$ For a line family $R$, define $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\prod_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto(\rho_M(A))_{M\in R}.$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching certificate
nodes.notes: Only retained mass and reached roots are required; no minimum-degree hypothesis is built into the interface.
nodes.statement_markdown: A rank-reaching certificate is $(G,R,D)$ where $G=(X,T,E)$ is a nonempty subgraph of $\mathcal I$, $R\subseteq T$, $D\in\mathbb Z$, $d\le D$, $|R|>D$, and $$\operatorname{rank}(\Phi_{R,D})<\dim V_D.$$ Every $L\in T$ must have more than $D$ distinct points $x$ such that $(x,L)\in E$ and $(x,M)\in E$ for some $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$.

nodes.label: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This remains the principal campaign obligation. The direct branch is necessary because graph-only reaching families can be expensive even on immediately decodable instances.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, there exist constants $C_\theta>0$, $0<a_\theta\le1$, and $K_\theta\ge1$ such that, whenever $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta(d/p)^{1-\theta},$$ either $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge a_\theta\epsilon$, or there is a rank-reaching certificate $(G,R,D)$ satisfying $$\mu(E)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear parameter slack
nodes.notes: The ratio is at most $K_\theta(d/p)^\theta/C_\theta$; increasing $C_\theta$ supplies all later loss absorption.
nodes.statement_markdown: After increasing $C_\theta$ as a function of $a_\theta,K_\theta,\theta$, every relation alternative satisfies $$D/(\epsilon p)\le a_\theta/[100(K_\theta+1)],\qquad D<p.$$

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: The cited interpolation steps supply nearby radicalization templates; the rank-general statement still needs a standalone implementation.
nodes.statement_markdown: In the relation alternative, there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$\rho_M(A)=0\quad(M\in R),\qquad A_Z\ne0.$$ Take the product of the distinct irreducible factors of a nonzero kernel element. Each selected restriction remains zero because $\mathbb F_p[t]$ is a domain. If the result were $Z$-independent, more than $D$ distinct line equations would divide a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D$. Finally, $D<p$ makes $Z$-dependence characteristic-safe.

nodes.label: Reached-root identity extension
nodes.notes: Distinct reached points give distinct roots of a restriction of degree at most $D$.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every $L\in T$, $$\rho_L(A)=A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0.$$ Indeed, each reached accepted point also lies on a selected line where $A$ vanishes, and both incident labels equal $f$ there. More than $D$ such roots force the identity.

nodes.label: Primitive factor allocation
nodes.notes: The 0007 and 0010 sources have enclosing verdict `revise`; they are used only as exact planning evidence.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the gcd of the $Z$-coefficients, $h=\deg H$, and $\delta=\operatorname{wdeg}B$. Then $B$ is primitive, squarefree, and $Z$-dependent, with $h+\delta\le D$. Delete the at most $h$ lines contained in $H=0$ and factor $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i.$$ Every $C_i$ depends on $Z$, and $$s\le\deg_ZB\le\delta/d\le D/d\le K_\theta.$$ The remaining lines admit a disjoint allocation $T=\bigsqcup_iT_i$ such that $$C_i(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))=0\quad(L\in T_i).$$

nodes.label: Characteristic-safe factor separability and resultants
nodes.notes: Small weighted degree is a sufficient separability criterion. For reducible $B$, the condition $B_Z\ne0$ alone does not imply $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Every allocated factor satisfies $$C_{i,Z}\ne0,
\qquad \gcd(C_i,C_{i,Z})=1,$$ because $C_i$ is irreducible, $Z$-dependent, and $\operatorname{wdeg}C_i\le D<p<dp$. More generally, if coprime $U,V$ have weighted degrees $u,v$ and $Z$-degrees $r,s$, respectively, then the number of graph lines on which both restrictions vanish identically is at most $$su+rv-drs.$$

nodes.label: Assigned-factor polar budget
nodes.notes: The factorwise source has an exact line audit but enclosing verdict `revise`; this node records the reusable bound without elevating its status.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Put $$\delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}C_i,
\qquad r_i=\deg_ZC_i,
\qquad \gamma_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_{i,Z}),$$ and $$\Xi_i=(r_i-1)\delta_i+r_i\gamma_i-dr_i(r_i-1).$$ If $b_i$ is the number of allocated lines on which $C_{i,Z}(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))$ vanishes identically, then $$b_i\le\min\{|T_i|,\Xi_i\},
\qquad \gamma_i\le\delta_i-d,
\qquad \Xi_i\le\delta_i^2/d-\delta_i.$$ Every other allocated line contains at most $\gamma_i$ accepted points where $C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))=0$.

nodes.label: Normalized factorwise ramification cleanup
nodes.notes: This replaces whole-relation cleanup and global peeling by an assigned-factor deletion charged directly to total mass.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Delete the content lines from AE-16, every identically ramified allocated line from AE-10, and every remaining accepted edge with $C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))=0$. If $E_{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the surviving edge set, then the deleted normalized mass satisfies $$\beta\le (D^2/d-D)/(p(p+1))+(D-d)/p\le a_\theta\epsilon/100.$$ Hence $$\mu(E_{\mathrm{cl}})\ge a_\theta\epsilon/2,$$ and every surviving edge assigned to $i$ satisfies $$C_i(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Heavy clean factor and simple seed
nodes.notes: Only total edge mass is used; connectivity and inherited vertex degrees are unnecessary.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Partition $E_{\mathrm{cl}}= igsqcup_iE_i$ by the assigned line factor and put $
u_i=\mu(E_i)$. Since $s\le K_	heta$, some $i$ satisfies $$
u_i\ge a_	heta\epsilon/(2K_	heta).$$ Moreover, AE-13 gives $$
u_i(p+1)>D\ge\delta_i.$$ Averaging the $E_i$-degrees over all $p^2$ points therefore yields a point $b$ incident to more than $\delta_i$ distinct lines of $T_i$, with $$C_i(b,f(b))=0,
\qquad C_{i,Z}(b,f(b))
e0.$$

nodes.label: Simple-pencil factor linearization
nodes.notes: No accept-verdict source states this exact standalone package. The proof uses formal implicit uniqueness and divides only by the nonzero scalar $C_Z(b,\alpha)$; no factorials occur.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be irreducible and $Z$-dependent with $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}C\le D<p$. Suppose $C(b,\alpha)=0$, $C_Z(b,\alpha)\ne0$, and more than $\Delta$ distinct lines $L_v(t)=b+tv$ carry polynomials $P_v$ of degree at most $d$ satisfying $$P_v(0)=\alpha,
\qquad C(b+tv,P_v(t))=0\text{ in }\mathbb F_p[t].$$ Then there are $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ and $u\in\mathbb F_p^\times$ such that $$C=u(Z-Q).$$ Applied at the seed of AE-18, this linearizes $C_i$.

nodes.label: Disconnected factor aggregation
nodes.notes: The irreducible factor is global, so all its disconnected clean pieces charge to the same polynomial without incidence mixing.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $C_i=u(Z-Q)$ be supplied by AE-19, and let $X_i$ be the point endpoints of $E_i$. Then $Q(x)=f(x)$ for every $x\in X_i$. Since $|E_i|\le(p+1)|X_i|$, $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge |X_i|/p^2\ge\mu(E_i)=\nu_i\ge a_\theta\epsilon/(2K_\theta).$$

nodes.label: Conditional fixed-theta algebraic engine
nodes.notes: The direct alternative of AE-12 already has the conclusion; AE-13 through AE-20 close its relation alternative.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, assuming AE-12, there are constants $C_\theta,c_\theta>0$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta(d/p)^{1-\theta}$$ implies $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\theta\epsilon$. One may take $$c_\theta=a_\theta/(2K_\theta).$$

nodes.label: Near-linear algebraic propagation engine
nodes.notes: Take $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. The endpoint remains blocked on AE-12 and on standalone proof records for the factorwise assembly and simple-pencil lift.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\eta<1$, there exist constants $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, and every accepted-incidence instance of density $\epsilon$, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta(d/p)^{1-\eta}$$ implies that one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Constant-loss core pruning
nodes.notes: This remains an off-path structural interface; its enclosing audit verdict is `revise`.
nodes.statement_markdown: Every accepted graph of mass $\epsilon$ contains a subgraph of mass at least $\epsilon/4$ and minimum degree at least $\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$.

nodes.label: Accepted component decoder
nodes.notes: This is the retained component-level algebraic baseline.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $G$ be a connected accepted subgraph of minimum degree $k$, let $\tau=|T|/[p(p+1)]$, and suppose $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,
\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2.$$ Then some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge k/(800p).$$

nodes.label: Whole-explainer square-root floor
nodes.notes: This is an architectural ceiling for the accepted component construction, not for rank-aware interpolation.
nodes.statement_markdown:
The AE-05 construction has $$D=\Theta(\sqrt{d\tau p^2/k}),
\qquad D<k,
\qquad \tau\ge k/(4p).$$ Consequently $k^2=\Omega(dp)$, so with $k=\Theta(\epsilon p)$ this route cannot reach below $\epsilon=\Omega((d/p)^{1/2})$.

nodes.label: Universal-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: A uniformly small graph-only reaching family cannot replace AE-12's decoder alternative.
nodes.statement_markdown: For suitable legal constant-label instances with $1/(2K)\le\epsilon\le2/K$, every line family reaching half the accepted points of every accepted line has size at least $$p/(32\epsilon),$$ although a constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Uniform-jet rank barrier
nodes.notes: The source audit is inexact with verdict `revise`; the statement is retained only as a diagnostic for raw uniform multiplicity counting.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For positive integers $s,D,n,h$ with $d\le D<p$ and $n>D$, put $$C_s(D,d)=\sum_{a+b<s}\max(D-a-db+1,0).$$ If raw counting gives $$\dim V_D>nC_s(D,d),
\qquad sh>D,$$ then $$h^2>dn/12.$$

nodes.label: Singular-seed guardrail
nodes.notes: This shows that the simple-root hypothesis in AE-19 cannot be discarded.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For legal choices with $d+1<p$, there is a primitive, squarefree, absolutely irreducible polynomial $$C=XZ+H(Y),
\qquad \operatorname{wdeg}C=d+1,$$ supporting more than $d+1$ compatible degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines through one common lift, while no total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ satisfies $C(X,Y,Q)=0$. At the common lift, $C_Z=0$.

nodes.label: Graph-only moment and fractional-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: The enclosing audit verdict is `revise`; this is off-path evidence about what AE-12 cannot be reduced to.
nodes.statement_markdown: Every raw accepted incidence graph is $K_{2,2}$-free. Moreover, for every prime $p$ and $101\le d<p$, there is a legal instance of density $\epsilon_0=d/p$ whose accepted carrier is connected and has full support, attains every point- and line-star lower envelope, and satisfies for $0<\vartheta\le1$ $$\vartheta p(p+1)/(d+1)\le\operatorname{OPT}_\vartheta\le\vartheta p(p+1)/(d-1),$$ while the polynomial $Q=0$ agrees with $f$ everywhere.

nodes.label: Asymmetric square-root decoder frontier
nodes.notes: The enclosing audit verdict is `revise`. This strengthens the component baseline but does not provide the bounded-weight alternative in AE-12.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let a nonempty accepted graph have point minimum degree $u$, line minimum degree $v$, $w=\min\{u,v\}$, and line measure $\tau$. If $$uv\ge2^{60}dp,
\qquad uw^2\ge2^{60}d\tau p^2,$$ then some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge v/(800p).$$

roadmaps.summary: Round 3 keeps the bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy as the principal open input and replaces the previous whole-relation cleanup-plus-peeling branch by a mass-only factorwise route. Rank deficiency yields a squarefree relation; reached roots extend it to all carrier lines; primitive factor allocation leaves at most $K_\theta$ factors; characteristic-safe resultants delete at most $(D^2/d-D)/(p(p+1))+(D-d)/p$ normalized mass. One factor then retains $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ mass, and point-degree averaging supplies a simple seed with more directions than its weighted degree. Formal implicit uniqueness and line-factor divisibility force that factor to be $Z-Q$, so all disconnected pieces aggregate to one global degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial. New researcher-0009 and researcher-0010 inputs strengthen the graph-only and asymmetric square-root diagnostics but do not establish the bounded-weight handoff. The endpoint remains blocked on AE-12 and on standalone proof records for the factorwise assembly and simple-pencil lift.
roadmaps.target_statement: Prove an algebraic interpolation-and-propagation lemma strong enough to preserve a near-linear power of the accepted incidence density over $\mathbb F_p^2$.
roadmaps.title: Algebraic propagation engine

roadmaps.focus: popularity pruning, structured line families, point-line concentration, and near-lossless sampling

messages.body_markdown: `IE-L-COMPONENT-LIFT` imports the generic whole-relation lift from `researcher-0001:P7.1`. For each component, $B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma)=0$ gives $Z-Q_\Gamma\mid B$; hence at most $\deg_ZB\le D/d$ distinct component polynomials occur, and edge pigeonholing yields one global $Q$. This adopts `E2E-21`--`E2E-23` and removes the former irreducible-factor seed obligation from the primary path; simple-root cleanup remains essential.
messages.subject: Component templates replace factor lift

messages.body_markdown: Researcher-0010 `[P8]` handles $u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d$. Accordingly, `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` is explicitly the complementary low-tail obligation, while `IE-R-FULL-DICHOTOMY` exports the unconditional decoder-or-rank-reaching interface needed by the other roadmaps. No source proves the residual $D\le K_\theta d$ statement.
messages.subject: High-tail and full-interface split

messages.body_markdown: Researcher-0009 strengthens the graph-only warning: one connected full-support carrier simultaneously attains every point- and line-star lower envelope, has fractional reaching optimum $\Theta(\vartheta p/\epsilon)$, and has the perfect decoder $Q=0$. Its auxiliary DRC estimate must also pay the concurrency correction in `IE-L-AUXILIARY-DRC`; at the cubic scale the resulting density-only root-rich bound is trivial. These are method barriers, not counterexamples to the target.
messages.subject: Sharper graph-only ceiling

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence graph
nodes.notes: All normalization is for uniform affine incidences in the fixed bivariate prime-field scope.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and, for every affine line $L$, a bijective affine parametrization $L:\mathbb F_p\to L$ and $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$. Define $$E_{\rm acc}=\{(L(t),L):P_L(t)=f(L(t))\},\qquad \rho=d/p,\qquad \epsilon=|E_{\rm acc}|/[p^2(p+1)],$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d}\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)].$$ For a nonempty $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq E_{\rm acc}$ put $$e(G)=|E|/[p^2(p+1)],\quad \mu(G)=|X|/p^2,\quad \tau(G)=|T|/[p(p+1)],$$ $$u(G)=\min_{x\in X}\deg_G(x),\qquad v(G)=\min_{L\in T}\deg_G(L).$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching structured family
nodes.notes: The definition allows $D\ge d$; the characteristic bound $D<p$ is derived only after the dichotomy.
nodes.statement_markdown: For an integer $D\ge d$, let $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\}$$ and $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto\bigl(A(M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ For $G=(X,T,E)$ define $$\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E,\ \exists M\in R\setminus\{L\},\ (x,M)\in E\}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching if $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $$\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<\dim V_D,$$ and $|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>D$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Accepted point-popularity tail
nodes.notes: Universally, $u_*\ge\lceil\epsilon(p+1)/2\rceil$; this lower bound alone recovers only the cubic scale.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Assume $\epsilon>0$. For $$a_x=|\{L:(x,L)\in E_{\rm acc}\}|,
\qquad \delta_j=[p^2(p+1)]^{-1}\sum_{x:a_x\ge j}a_x,$$ define $$u_*=\max\{j\in\{1,\ldots,p+1\}:\delta_j\ge\epsilon/2\}.$$

nodes.label: High-tail asymmetric core
nodes.notes: The indexed source step is conditional and its enclosing audit verdict is `revise`; the harness determines status.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If $$u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d,$$ then the incidences supported on $\{x:a_x\ge u_*\}$ contain a nonempty accepted graph $G_*$ with $u=u(G_*)$, $v=v(G_*)$, $\tau=\tau(G_*)$, and $w=\min\{u,v\}$ satisfying $$u\ge u_*/3,\qquad v\ge\epsilon p/16,$$ $$uv\ge2^{60}dp,
\qquad uw^2\ge2^{60}d\tau p^2.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless asymmetric reaching sample
nodes.notes: This is the asymmetric cardinality sampler; its enclosing audit verdict is `revise`.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be nonempty, let $u=u(G)$, $v=v(G)$, $t=|T|$, $\tau=\tau(G)$, and $w=\min\{u,v\}$. If $$uv\ge2^{60}dp,
\qquad uw^2\ge2^{60}d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\tau\ge u/[4(p+1)],\qquad \mu(G)\ge v/(4p),\qquad w^2\ge2^{57}dp,$$ and there is $R\subseteq T$ such that $$4t/u\le|R|\le16t/u,
\qquad |R|\ge p,$$ and $$|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>\deg_G(L)/2$$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Asymmetric incidence decoder
nodes.notes: This packages interpolation, extension, cleanup, pruning, and recovery from the asymmetric sample.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under the hypotheses of `IE-L-ASYMMETRIC-SAMPLE`, there exists one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ such that $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge v/(800p).$$

nodes.label: High-popularity-tail decoder
nodes.notes: No universal tail estimate strong enough for an exponent above $1/3$ is asserted.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $$u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d,$$ then one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\epsilon/12800.$$

nodes.label: Residual bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal unresolved incidence obligation. The direct branch is essential because label-blind reaching families can be large even for perfectly decodable tables.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$ there exist $C_\theta,K_\theta\ge1$ and $a_\theta,c_\theta>0$ such that, if $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta},
\qquad u_*\epsilon^2<2^{70}d,$$ then either $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\theta\epsilon,$$ or there exist $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq E_{\rm acc}$, $R\subseteq T$, and an integer $d\le D\le K_\theta d$ such that $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon$$ and $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Export the unconditional dichotomy
nodes.notes: This node aligns the residual incidence obligation with the unconditional interface used by the peer roadmaps.
nodes.statement_markdown:
With $c_\theta^*=\min\{c_\theta,1/12800\}$, the high-tail theorem and residual dichotomy imply that $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta}$$ yields either $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\theta^*\epsilon$$ or a rank-reaching $(G,R,D)$ with $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless parameter gate
nodes.notes: Increasing $C_\theta$ preserves the dichotomy and introduces no hypothesis beyond $d<p$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Enlarge $C_\theta$ until $C_\theta\ge16K_\theta/a_\theta$. In the structured branch, $$D/p\le(K_\theta/C_\theta)\epsilon\le a_\theta\epsilon/16,
\qquad D<p,$$ and therefore $$(D/p)^2+3D/p\le a_\theta\epsilon/4.$$

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: Radicalization preserves every selected graph identity; $|R|>D$ rules out a base-only relation after $D<p$ is known.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the structured branch there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\not\equiv0,
\qquad A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\quad(M\in R).$$

nodes.label: Reached-root extension
nodes.notes: The cited accepted step supplies the same degree-versus-distinct-roots argument.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every $L\in T$, the more than $D$ points in $\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)$ are roots of the degree-at-most-$D$ polynomial $A(L(t),P_L(t))$. Hence $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0\qquad(L\in T).$$

nodes.label: Primitive separable reduction
nodes.notes: Content removal and vertical separability are kept explicit before resultant counting.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content in $Z$, $B$ is primitive in $Z$, $h=\deg H$, and $\delta=\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}B$. Then $B$ is squarefree and $Z$-dependent, $$d\le\delta,
\qquad h+\delta\le D<pd,
\qquad \gcd(B,B_Z)=1.$$ At most $h$ line vertices satisfy $H(L(t))\equiv0$; every other line vertex satisfies $$B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Weighted vertical cleanup count
nodes.notes: The formula contains only literal TeX backslashes and no control characters.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $r=\deg_ZB$. The number of content-trivial or identically $B_Z$-ramified graph lines is at most $$h+(2r-1)\delta-dr^2\le h+\delta^2/d-\delta\le D^2/d-D.$$ On every other graph line, $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is nonzero of degree at most $\delta-d\le D-d$. Deleting every nonsimple accepted incidence therefore costs at most $$(D^2/d-D)/[p(p+1)]+(D-d)/p\le(D/p)^2+D/p.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless global cleanup and peeling
nodes.notes: Every peeled edge is charged once to the removed vertex; the two shore minima are stated explicitly.
nodes.statement_markdown:
After vertical cleanup, iteratively delete every point or line vertex of current degree at most $D$. Peeling costs less than $2D/p$. A nonempty $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ remains with $$e(G_1)\ge a_\theta\epsilon/2,
\qquad u(G_1)>D,
\qquad v(G_1)>D.$$ Every $L\in T_1$ satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every $x\in X_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Componentwise whole-relation lift
nodes.notes: The generic implication is exact-audited in a source with enclosing verdict `revise`; it replaces the former seed-factor obligation on the primary route.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every connected component $\Gamma$ of $G_1$, there is $Q_\Gamma\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q_\Gamma\le d$ such that $$B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))\equiv0,
\qquad Q_\Gamma(x)=f(x)\quad(x\in X(\Gamma)).$$

nodes.label: Bounded component-template compression
nodes.notes: This is the polynomial remainder theorem followed by distinct linear-divisor counting.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $\mathcal Q=\{Q_\Gamma:\Gamma\text{ a component of }G_1\}$. For every $Q\in\mathcal Q$, $$B(X,Y,Q)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Z-Q(X,Y)\mid B(X,Y,Z).$$ Distinct $Q$ give distinct monic linear divisors, so $$1\le|\mathcal Q|\le\deg_ZB\le\left\lfloor D/d\right\rfloor\le K_\theta.$$

nodes.label: Vinh-free component aggregation
nodes.notes: Components producing the same polynomial are combined before the edge pigeonhole.
nodes.statement_markdown: Partition $E_1$ by the value of $Q_\Gamma$. Some $Q\in\mathcal Q$ carries an edge set $E_Q$ with $$|E_Q|/[p^2(p+1)]\ge e(G_1)/|\mathcal Q|\ge a_\theta\epsilon/(2K_\theta).$$ If $X_Q$ is the union of its component point sets, then $Q=f$ on $X_Q$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge|X_Q|/p^2\ge|E_Q|/[p^2(p+1)]\ge a_\theta\epsilon/(2K_\theta).$$

nodes.label: Close all branches and exponents
nodes.notes: The only genuinely new mathematical bottleneck on this path is the residual bounded-weight dichotomy; downstream drafting nodes still require the harness's exact audits.
nodes.statement_markdown: For fixed $\eta>0$, set $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Since $0<\rho<1$, $$\rho^{1-\eta}\ge\rho^{1-\theta}.$$ The high-tail, residual direct, and structured branches yield constants $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\rho^{1-\eta}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate line-versus-point soundness
nodes.notes: The endpoint recovers one polynomial, not merely a list. Work state does not assert proof verification.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, integer $100<d<p$, function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and degree-at-most-$d$ affine-line table, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta(d/p)^{1-\eta}$$ implies the existence of one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Baseline two-sided popularity pruning
nodes.notes: This preserves the useful round-2 constant-mass core.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If an accepted carrier $G$ has $e(G)=\delta>0$ and $\tau(G)\le\sigma$, put $k_0=\lfloor\delta p/100\rfloor$. There is $G_0\subseteq G$ such that $$e(G_0)\ge\delta/4,
\qquad u(G_0),v(G_0)\ge k_0,
\qquad \delta/4\le\tau(G_0)\le\sigma.$$

nodes.label: Accepted component concentration and sampling
nodes.notes: Both inputs have independently accepted audits and give the cardinality-based baseline.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be connected with $u(G),v(G)\ge k$, $t=|T|$, and $\tau=\tau(G)$. If $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,
\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\mu(G),\tau\ge k/(4p),$$ and there is $R\subseteq T$ such that $$4t/k\le|R|\le16t/k,
\qquad |\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>\deg_G(L)/2$$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Accepted component decoder
nodes.notes: This is the accepted component-level recovery theorem retained from round 2.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under the hypotheses of `IE-L-COMP-SAMPLE`, there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ such that $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge k/(800p).$$

nodes.label: Component-support square-root ceiling
nodes.notes: Thus component localization alone cannot reach the near-linear exponent.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $0<k\le C\epsilon p$, $\tau\ge k/(4p)$, and $$k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\epsilon^2\ge[C_*/(4C^2)](d/p).$$

nodes.label: Exact-template direct decoders
nodes.notes: These lemmas consume an already extracted structured family; they do not create the templates.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let disjoint line families $T_1,\ldots,T_r$ carry normalized accepted mass $\delta$ and total line measure $\tau$, and suppose $$P_L(t)=Q_j(L(t))\qquad(L\in T_j)$$ for total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials $Q_j$. If $\alpha=\max_j\Pr_x[Q_j(x)=f(x)]$, then $$\delta\le\alpha\tau+\sqrt{r\alpha\tau/(p+1)}.$$ Hence $r\le\delta(p+1)$ implies $\alpha\ge\delta/4$. If all labels are constant and $\mu_0=\max_a\Pr_x[f(x)=a]$, then $$\delta\le\mu_0\tau+\sqrt{\tau/(p+1)},$$ so $\delta\ge2\sqrt{\tau/(p+1)}$ implies $\mu_0\ge\delta/(2\tau)\ge\delta/2$.

nodes.label: Integral reaching-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: This refutes a universal small graph-only cover, not soundness.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$ there is a legal table with $$1/(2K)\le\epsilon\le2/K$$ such that every line subset reaching half of every accepted line has $$|R|\ge Kp/16\ge p/(32\epsilon),$$ while $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\epsilon/2.$$

nodes.label: Exact point-line star envelopes
nodes.notes: The star order ranges incorporate the verifier correction; no unqualified $\Theta(\epsilon^2)$ claim is made near $\epsilon=1/p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $a_x$ and $b_L$ be the accepted point and line degrees. For $\mu=k+\lambda$, where $k=\lfloor\mu\rfloor$ and $0\le\lambda<1$, put $$J_s(\mu)=(1-\lambda)(k)_s+\lambda(k+1)_s.$$ Then $$\Gamma_s^P=\mathbb E_x[(a_x)_s]/(p+1)_s\ge J_s((p+1)\epsilon)/(p+1)_s\qquad(0\le s\le p+1),$$ $$\Gamma_s^L=\mathbb E_L[(b_L)_s]/(p)_s\ge J_s(p\epsilon)/(p)_s\qquad(0\le s\le p),$$ and the with-replacement moments satisfy $\widetilde\Gamma_r^P,\widetilde\Gamma_r^L\ge\epsilon^r$ for $r\ge1$. In particular, $$\Gamma_2^P=\epsilon^2-\epsilon(1-\epsilon)/p+\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)/[p(p+1)].$$

nodes.label: Connected regular reaching obstruction
nodes.notes: The enclosing audit verdict is `revise`; the corrected statement concerns the optimum, not every feasible weighting.
nodes.statement_markdown: There is a connected, full-support legal table with $\epsilon_0=d/p$, every line of accepted degree $d$, exactly $pd$ points of accepted degree $d+1$, every other point of degree $d$, and $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=1$. It attains both star envelopes in `IE-L-STAR-ENVELOPES`. For $0<\vartheta\le1$, let $\operatorname{OPT}_\vartheta$ be the minimum total nonnegative line weight giving every accepted line at least $\vartheta d$ capped coverage through other accepted lines. Then $$\vartheta p(p+1)/(d+1)\le\operatorname{OPT}_\vartheta\le\vartheta p(p+1)/(d-1)=\Theta(\vartheta p/\epsilon_0).$$

nodes.label: Bounded-order star-energy obstruction
nodes.notes: These examples lie below every fixed target trigger and therefore do not refute near-linear soundness.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed integer $S\ge2$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, there is a legal constant-label instance with $d=101$ such that $$\epsilon=\Theta(\log p/[p\log\log p]),
\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_{101}(f)<2/p,$$ every affine line supports acceptance, and $$\Gamma_s^P\le2^{s+2}(S-1)\epsilon^s\qquad(2\le s\le S).$$

nodes.label: Compatibility-graph DRC with concurrency correction
nodes.notes: Raw $K_{2,2}$-freeness is recorded but is not transferred to the auxiliary graph.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Every raw accepted affine incidence graph is $K_{2,2}$-free. Let $H$ be the graph on the $N=p(p+1)$ affine lines, joining distinct nonparallel lines when both accept their intersection. With $\mu_0=(p+1)\epsilon$ and average degree $\bar\Delta$, $$e(H)=\sum_x\binom{a_x}{2},
\qquad \bar\Delta\ge p\mu_0(\mu_0-1)/(p+1).$$ For an integer $1\le t\le\lfloor\bar\Delta\rfloor$, put $$M_t(H)=\frac{\sum_L\binom{\deg_H(L)}t}{\binom Nt}.$$ Some $t$-line seed has at least $$M_t(H)\ge N\binom{\lfloor\bar\Delta\rfloor}t/\binom Nt$$ common neighbors; if $\mu_0\ge2$ and $\bar\Delta\ge2t+2$, then $M_t(H)\ge N(\epsilon^2/4)^t$. For every integer $1\le h\le t$, at least $$M_t(H)-\binom t2(p+1)/(t-h+1)$$ common neighbors meet the seed lines in at least $h$ distinct points.

nodes.label: Density-only DRC root-budget barrier
nodes.notes: This limits only the displayed density-only certificate; it is not an impossibility result for algebra-aware DRC.
nodes.statement_markdown: Put $$D_t=16(\lfloor\sqrt{dt}\rfloor+1).$$ A transfer requiring $h>D_t$ with $h\le t$ requires $t>D_t$ and hence $t>256d$. For fixed $d,t,C$ and $$\epsilon_p=C(d/p)^{1/3},$$ $$N(\epsilon_p^2/4)^t=O_{C,d,t}(p^{2-2t/3})\longrightarrow0.$$ If $t>D_t$ and $h=D_t+1$, substituting this density term into the concurrency-corrected bound of `IE-L-AUXILIARY-DRC` is eventually negative and therefore supplies no root-rich target.

nodes.label: Singular common lifts do not linearize
nodes.notes: This accepted obstruction explains why the $B_Z\ne0$ cleanup hypothesis cannot be discarded.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $d\ge101$ and $p>4d+1$, there is an absolutely irreducible $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree $D=2d$ supporting $(p-1)/2>D$ distinct degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines, while no $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ satisfies $$C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0.$$ Every vertically ramified lift on those graph lines is singular on $C=0$.

roadmaps.summary: Round 3 adds the asymmetric popularity-tail chain: if $u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d$, a two-sided high-tail core, a $\Theta(|T|/u)$ reaching sample, and the asymmetric decoder yield agreement at least $\epsilon/12800$. The central incidence obligation is therefore isolated to the complementary low-tail regime and then repackaged as the unconditional bounded-weight interface required by peer roadmaps. Exact point- and line-star envelopes, the connected regular carrier, integral and fractional reaching obstructions, bounded-order modal examples, and concurrency-corrected auxiliary DRC explain why label-blind sampling or fixed-order energy cannot prove that interface. The structured branch still asks for accepted mass $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ and $D=O_\theta(d)$; this makes vertical cleanup and degree-$D$ peeling near-lossless. The downstream route is shortened using the peer `E2E-21`--`E2E-23` idea: lift the common cleaned relation on each component, observe that each component polynomial contributes a divisor $Z-Q$ of the same $B$, bound the number of distinct component templates by $\deg_ZB\le D/d$, and pigeonhole edges. This replaces the former factor-partition and seed-factor-linearization path. The residual bounded-weight dichotomy remains open, and downstream drafting nodes remain subject to exact source and verifier checks.
roadmaps.target_statement: Convert local line-versus-point agreement into a structured affine-plane incidence configuration with only a $(d/p)^{o(1)}$ loss.
roadmaps.title: Incidence concentration engine

roadmaps.focus: a complete KTZ-style dependency chain ending in one global polynomial and exponent $1-o(1)$

messages.body_markdown: Round 3 can bypass the standalone seed-factor lift in `AE-19`. After `E2E-20`, apply the generic whole-relation lift componentwise. Every resulting $Q_\Gamma$ satisfies $B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma)=0$, so $Z-Q_\Gamma$ divides the common $B$; hence there are at most $\deg_ZB\le D/d$ distinct component polynomials. Edge pigeonholing then gives one global polynomial. Please audit `E2E-21`–`E2E-23` as a standalone combined lemma.
messages.subject: Component-template compression replaces seed-factor lift

messages.body_markdown: `E2E-15` remains the principal incidence obligation: retain $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ accepted mass while producing a rank-reaching relation with $D\le K_\theta d$, or decode directly. The connected carrier of researcher-0009 has optimal fractional reaching cost $\Theta(\vartheta p/\epsilon)$ and a $K_{2,2}$-free raw graph despite the perfect decoder $Q=0$, so connectivity, moments, fractional covers, and raw DRC cannot replace the label-aware alternative.
messages.subject: Bounded-weight dichotomy still controls the exponent

messages.body_markdown: The bound $D=O_\theta(d)$ now has a cleaner second use. Besides making the cleanup loss $O_\theta(d/p)$ absorbable, it bounds the number of distinct component lifts by $\deg_ZB\le D/d=O_\theta(1)$. Thus `E2E-21`–`E2E-23` aggregate one polynomial by elementary edge pigeonholing and no longer require a globally heavy irreducible factor or a separate simple-seed factor-linearization theorem.
messages.subject: Bounded weight also bounds component templates

nodes.label: Bivariate line-versus-point instance
nodes.notes: The scope is exactly $m=2$, prime field, and integer $100<d<p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$ for every affine line $L$. Define $$\rho=\frac d p,\qquad \epsilon=\Pr_{L,\,x\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)],\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d}\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)].$$

nodes.label: Accepted graph and completion predicate
nodes.notes: The normalization converts edge mass directly into a lower bound on point agreement.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $$E_{\rm acc}=\{(x,L):x\in L,\ P_L(x)=f(x)\}.$$ For an accepted subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$ put $$e(G)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)}.$$ For $c>0$, let $\mathsf{Done}_c$ mean that some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ satisfies $\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c\epsilon$.

nodes.label: Fixed-exponent reduction
nodes.notes: It is enough to establish the engine for $0<\theta\le1/4$.
nodes.statement_markdown: For fixed $\eta>0$, put $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Since $0<\rho<1$, $$0<\theta\le\frac14,\qquad \rho^{1-\eta}\ge\rho^{1-\theta}.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ component measures
nodes.notes: This begins the independently accepted component-level KTZ chain.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a connected accepted graph of minimum degree $k$, and put $\tau=|T|/[p(p+1)]$. If $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\frac{|X|}{p^2}\ge\frac{k}{4p},\qquad \tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ reaching family
nodes.notes: The selector is cardinality-based and local to one connected component.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `E2E-04`, there is $R\subseteq T$ such that $$\frac{4|T|}{k}\le|R|\le\frac{16|T|}{k},\qquad |R|\ge p+1,$$ and every $L\in T$ has more than half of its accepted neighbors incident to a line of $R\setminus\{L\}$.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ weighted interpolant
nodes.notes: The interpolation degree depends on the cardinality of the reaching family.
nodes.statement_markdown: Put $$D=16\left(\left\lfloor\sqrt{d|R|}\right\rfloor+1\right).$$ There is a nonzero squarefree $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ with $\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D$, $A_Z\not\equiv0$, and $$A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\qquad(M\in R).$$ Moreover, $D/k<1/5000$ and $D<k\le p<|R|$.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ root extension
nodes.notes: More than $D$ reached roots force each remaining restriction identity.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every $L\in T$, $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ characteristic-safe cleanup
nodes.notes: The resultant argument is valid throughout the campaign's prime-field range.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content in $Z$. Then $B$ is squarefree and has total degree below $p$. There is a formal directional derivative $\mathcal D$ with $\gcd(B,\mathcal DB)=1$ and an exceptional set satisfying $$|E_{\rm exc}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$ Outside $E_{\rm exc}$, the $B$-identity holds and $\mathcal DB$ is nonzero at every retained accepted incidence.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ clean core
nodes.notes: Connectivity may fragment during the peeling operation.
nodes.statement_markdown: One has $$\frac{|E_{\rm exc}|}{|E|}<\frac1{4000}.$$ Peeling vertices below $k_1=\lfloor k/100\rfloor$ leaves a nonempty accepted graph $G_1$ of minimum degree at least $k_1$.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ simple roots
nodes.notes: Two retained directions convert generic derivative nonvanishing into vertical simplicity.
nodes.statement_markdown: Every point vertex $x$ of $G_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ component decoder
nodes.notes: The conclusion is one polynomial, not a list.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `E2E-04`, there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Conditional square-root frontier
nodes.notes: Local agreement does not itself imply the required small-component hypothesis.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $k_0=\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$. If a component of the KTZ-pruned core has line measure $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$ and $$\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000\cdot2^{40}\Lambda}\left(\frac d p\right)^{1/2},$$ then one degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/160000$.

nodes.label: Graph-only sparsification obstruction
nodes.notes: These examples have immediate decoders and therefore force, rather than refute, the decode branch in `E2E-15`.
nodes.statement_markdown: There are legal constant-label tables with $\epsilon\asymp1/K$ for which every family reaching half of every accepted line has size $\Omega(p/\epsilon)$ although a constant polynomial has agreement $\Omega(\epsilon)$. Moreover, at $\epsilon=d/p$ there is a connected full-support legal table with perfect decoder $Q=0$, raw accepted graph $K_{2,2}$-free, and fractional reaching optimum $$\frac{\vartheta p(p+1)}{d+1}\le\operatorname{OPT}_{\vartheta}\le\frac{\vartheta p(p+1)}{d-1}=\Theta\!\left(\frac{\vartheta p}{\epsilon}\right).$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching relation interface
nodes.notes: Unlike the round-2 definition, this does not assume $D<p$; that inequality is derived at `E2E-16`.
nodes.statement_markdown: For an integer $D\ge d$, put $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\},$$ $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto\bigl(A(M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching when $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<\dim V_D$, and every $L\in T$ has more than $D$ accepted neighbors $x$ for which some $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$ also satisfies $(x,M)\in E$.

nodes.label: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal open incidence bottleneck. The direct-decoder branch is indispensable by `E2E-13`.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, there exist $C_\theta,K_\theta\ge1$ and $a_\theta,c_\theta>0$ such that, whenever $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta},$$ either $\mathsf{Done}_{c_\theta}$ holds, or there is a rank-reaching tuple $(G,R,D)$ satisfying $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,\qquad D\le K_\theta d.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear parameter and loss gate
nodes.notes: Increasing $C_\theta$ is harmless; if the trigger exceeds one, the implication is vacuous.
nodes.statement_markdown: Enlarge $C_\theta$ until $K_\theta/C_\theta\le a_\theta/16$. In the relation branch, $$\frac{D}{\epsilon p}\le\frac{K_\theta}{C_\theta}\rho^\theta\le\frac{a_\theta}{16}.$$ Consequently, $$D<p,\qquad \left(\frac Dp\right)^2+3\frac Dp\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{2}.$$

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: The abstract rank-kernel formulation still needs a standalone exact audit.
nodes.statement_markdown: For the rank-reaching tuple, there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\not\equiv0,\qquad A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\quad(M\in R).$$ Indeed, take the squarefree radical of a nonzero kernel element; $|R|>D$ excludes a $Z$-independent kernel element, and $D<p$ makes every nonconstant $Z$-dependence separable.

nodes.label: Rank-reaching root extension
nodes.notes: This is the accepted reached-root argument with the rank-reaching interface substituted for the cardinality selector.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every line vertex $L\in T$, $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Whole-relation vertical cleanup
nodes.notes: The bounded-weight gate makes the exact $O(D/p)$ cleanup loss absorbable below $\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content in $Z$. Then $B$ is squarefree, primitive and $Z$-dependent, with $\operatorname{wdeg}B\le D<p$ and $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. There is $E_{\rm exc}\subseteq E$ such that $$|E_{\rm exc}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$ Every line incident to $E\setminus E_{\rm exc}$ satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every retained edge $(x,L)$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Global simple-root peeling
nodes.notes: Exceptional deletion costs at most $(D/p)^2+D/p$; peeling both shores at degree $D$ costs less than $2D/p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Delete $E_{\rm exc}$ and iteratively delete every point or line vertex of current degree at most $D$. The resulting nonempty accepted graph $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ satisfies $$e(G_1)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2}\epsilon,\qquad \operatorname{mindeg}(G_1)>D.$$ Every $L\in T_1$ satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every $x\in X_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Componentwise whole-relation lift
nodes.notes: The generic component interface is exact-audited but belongs to a source with overall revise verdict; a fresh standalone audit remains needed.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every connected component $\Gamma$ of $G_1$, there is $Q_\Gamma\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q_\Gamma\le d$ such that $$B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))\equiv0,
\qquad Q_\Gamma(x)=f(x)\quad(x\in X(\Gamma)).$$

nodes.label: Bounded component-template compression
nodes.notes: This elementary remainder-theorem argument replaces the former heavy-factor and simple-seed factor-linearization nodes.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $\mathcal Q$ be the set of distinct polynomials $Q_\Gamma$ from `E2E-21`. For every $Q\in\mathcal Q$, the identity $B(X,Y,Q)=0$ implies $$Z-Q(X,Y)\mid B(X,Y,Z).$$ Distinct $Q$ give distinct monic irreducible divisors, so $$1\le|\mathcal Q|\le\deg_ZB\le\left\lfloor\frac Dd\right\rfloor\le K_\theta.$$

nodes.label: Vinh-free aggregation to one polynomial
nodes.notes: Disconnected components sharing the same component lift are charged to the same algebraic polynomial.
nodes.statement_markdown: Partition $E_1$ by the polynomial $Q_\Gamma$ assigned to its component. Some $Q\in\mathcal Q$ carries normalized edge mass at least $$\frac{e(G_1)}{|\mathcal Q|}\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon.$$ If $X_Q$ is the union of its component point sets and $E_Q$ the corresponding edges, then $Q=f$ on $X_Q$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{|X_Q|}{p^2}\ge\frac{|E_Q|}{p^2(p+1)}\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon.$$ Together with the direct branch of `E2E-15`, this proves $\mathsf{Done}_{c_\theta^*}$ for $$c_\theta^*=\min\left\{c_\theta,\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\right\}.$$

nodes.label: Close every fixed exponent
nodes.notes: All constants depend only on the fixed exponent parameter.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$, there are $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\rho^{1-\eta}$$ implies that some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ satisfies $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Uniform exact-linear endpoint is false
nodes.notes: This does not refute any fixed-$\eta$ trigger because the counterexamples lie below $(d/p)^{1-\eta}$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every absolute $C,c>0$, there are arbitrarily large primes $p$ and legal instances with $d=101$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C\frac d p,
\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_d(f)<c\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Accepted singular-lift obstruction
nodes.notes: The intentionally refuted bundle in researcher-0006:P12 is not used as positive evidence. This node shows why `E2E-19` must certify simple roots.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p>4d+1$ and $D=2d$, there is an absolutely irreducible $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree $D$ supporting more than $D$ distinct degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines, while no $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ satisfies $C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0$. Every vertically ramified lift on the supported graphs is singular.

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate soundness
nodes.notes: The principal mathematical bottleneck is `E2E-15`; the generalized rank-kernel, cleanup-transfer, and component-template chain also awaits standalone exact audits. Work states do not assert proof status.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, and every legal bivariate line table, $$\operatorname{Agr}_{\rm LVP}(f,P)\ge C_\eta\left(\frac d p\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies that there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\operatorname{Agr}_{\rm LVP}(f,P).$$

roadmaps.summary: Round 3 retains the independently accepted KTZ component chain `E2E-04`–`E2E-12`, whose available unconditional machinery still stops at a conditional square-root frontier. The near-linear spine is `E2E-15`–`E2E-24`: a label-aware rank-or-decode dichotomy must retain $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ mass while producing weighted degree $D=O_\theta(d)$. The rank-reaching definition now correctly allows $D\ge d$, with $D<p$ derived downstream. The main structural simplification is `E2E-21`–`E2E-23`: lift the common cleaned relation separately on every connected component, observe that each resulting $Q_\Gamma$ contributes the divisor $Z-Q_\Gamma$ of the same polynomial $B$, and hence bound the number of distinct component polynomials by $\deg_ZB\le D/d$. Elementary edge pigeonholing then yields one global polynomial across all components, avoiding both Vinh mixing and the former standalone irreducible seed-factor lift. The target remains blocked on `E2E-15` and standalone audits of the generalized algebraic transfers; the uniform $Cd/p$ endpoint remains separately refuted.
roadmaps.target_statement: Prove that soundness at least $(d/p)^{1-o(1)}$ yields agreement with one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial for $100<d<p$ over $\mathbb F_p$.
roadmaps.title: End-to-end soundness chain
